primary_task: Search a .burp project file for response headers/bodies or audit findings by running Burp Suite Professional headless through a wrapper script.

requirements.name: Burp Suite Professional
requirements.evidence: This skill **delegates parsing to Burp Suite Professional** - it does not parse .burp files directly. **Required:** 1. **Burp Suite Professional** - Must be installed (portswigger.net)
requirements.basis: other hosts are refused (for example huggingface, Microsoft Learn and Azure, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA); portswigger.net is not among the open hosts (only PyPI, npm, GitHub, Ubuntu apt archives, NuGet and the Go module proxy) and Burp Pro is commercial software in none of those registries

requirements.name: burpsuite-project-file-parser extension
requirements.evidence: Download from github.com/BuffaloWill/burpsuite-project-file-parser ... In Burp Suite: Extender -> Extensions -> Add
requirements.basis: GitHub (github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com) ... are open (but it only runs inside Burp Pro)

requirements.name: Java (BURP_JAVA) and burpsuite_pro.jar (BURP_JAR)
requirements.evidence: The script uses environment variables ...: BURP_JAVA: Path to Java executable; BURP_JAR: Path to burpsuite_pro.jar
requirements.basis: Java is apt-installable, but burpsuite_pro.jar ships only with the Burp Pro install (see above); no manifest sentence provides it

requirements.name: a .burp project file
requirements.basis: The manifest does not say; would need the user to put the project file in the working directory

requirements.name: jq
requirements.basis: bash: install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, ...)

notes: The document says it does not parse .burp itself, so no alternative exists. A Burp Pro licence is implied (not stated, not counted). Linux paths are given, so the OS is not the blocker. If the user supplied a Burp install in the working directory the verdict would be ACHIEVABLE, but the manifest grants no such thing.
